The '''B2-series super battle droid''' or '''B2 super battle droid (SBD)''' was an upgraded version of the [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droid]], with superior armament and [[Armor/Legends|armor]]. They were manufactured after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] proved the need for stronger droids. B2s were used by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]], and later, on a much larger scale, the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. Some units were later reactivated on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]] by [[Gizor Dellso]] and other members of the [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|Separatist holdouts]], and the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] also used some B2 units during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:Battle_droids_on_Geonosis.jpg|thumb|left|180px|B2 super battle droids and B1 battle droids fighting during the First Battle of Geonosis.]]
One of the main design flaws of the standard [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droid]] was its reliance on a [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|Droid Control Ship]] to provide a signal; if the ships were disabled, the [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] would become useless. To remedy this, the super battle [[Droid/Legends|droid]] did not rely on such a signal and had a greater capacity for independence. However, the droid still operated best with a command signal. Otherwise, they tended to forget about enemies as soon as they moved out of visual range. Additionally, the sturdy [[Duranium/Legends|duranium]] and [[Phrik/Legends|phrik]] frame of the super battle droid was larger and more heavily armored than those of a B1.<ref name="Super battle droid droid in the Databank">{{DB|droid|superbattledroid|super battle droid}}''<nowiki/>''</ref>

Unlike its predecessor, the B2's delicate processing unit and signal receptor were buried deep inside the torso, offering much more protection from enemy fire. Small fully-automatic dual [[Blaster cannon/Legends|blaster cannons]] were mounted on their right forearms or even both forearms as seen in the [[Unidentified B2 super battle droid/Legends|Mission to Rugosa]]. In some cases, the weapons were replaced with a [[TriShot]] weapon system. The [[B2-HA super battle droid/Legends|B2-HA series super battle droid's]] left forearm was replaced by a [[Missile launcher/Legends|rocket launcher]]. They could use external weaponry (except in rocket launcher configuration), though their large hands had difficulty with more minor [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]]. Instead, they were equipped with special blasters that only responded to signal emitters built into the hands. For the sake of efficiency, they used many B1 parts. Their feet were also outfitted with specialized equipment for challenging terrains, such as climbing claws.<ref name="Super battle droid droid in the Databank" /> Their arms also were modular, capable of exchanging their blaster cannons for other specialized weaponry.
<div style="float: right">[[File:B2Lineup-SWE.png|thumb|200px|B2-HA battle droid lineup.]]</div>

When they were not using their built-in blaster cannons, they had their right forearm locked upright.<ref name="AOTC" /> A group of B2 units were modified to include [[swamp gas]] sprayers before being deployed on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]]. Other modified units utilized mortar launchers, standing repeating blaster cannons, built-in flamethrowers instead of blaster cannons, and rode upon [[Orray/Legends|orrays]].

As heavy [[Infantry/Legends|infantry]] droids, B2s could take much more punishment than their flimsy predecessors. Even after being defeated, they could detach their torsos and keep up an attack, although this was detrimental to their combat skill. Some models seemingly suffered low heat tolerance despite such traits and were subject to bursting into flame upon contact.<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref>

Most post-[[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]] B2 droids were capable of communicating with each other using an oversimplified version of [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]].

==History==
===Clone Wars===
{{Quote|They've sent in the supers!|Various [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] troopers|<ref name="BF2" />}}
The B2 was preceded by the lesser-used prototype [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|beta version]].<ref name="SWGB:CC">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]''</ref> Soon after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], the Trade Federation was [[Trade Federation Research Station|researching]] a new type of battle droid. [[Commando/Legends|Commandos]] from the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]] [[Attack on the Trade Federation Research Station|seized]] the research facility and discovered the data about this new battle droid.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I: Battle for Naboo">Research about the SBD was stolen during a raid, chronicled in a bonus mission in the video game ''[[Star Wars: Episode I: Battle for Naboo]]''.</ref>

During their first deployment at the [[Kashyyyk Trade Rebellion]] in [[28 BBY/Legends|28 BBY]], the new B2 designs proved to be a match for the local [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] warriors.<ref name="Battlefront">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront]]''</ref>

[[File:BarrissSBD.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Barriss Offee/Legends|Barriss Offee]] strikes down a B2 super battle droid on [[Drongar/Legends|Drongar]].]]
Super battle droids saw use throughout the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] as soldiers for the Confederacy along with its smaller cousins and the dreaded [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]]. Most super battle droids wore an unpainted dull silver tone, likely to differentiate them from the tan coloration the Confederacy used for its standard battle droids, or perhaps due to varying manufacturers. On occasion, they would be painted with green markings for camouflage.<ref name="Star Wars: Clone Wars">''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]''</ref>

Some Super Battle Droids were used as scouts to observe the plains of [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], mostly because of their brute strength and their ability to destroy modest ground targets. This pleased many of the local Geonosians affiliated with the CIS, thus sometimes using the B2s as "spire guards."

[[File:Camo_super_battle_droid.jpg|thumb|150px|A camouflaged super battle droid.]]
The droids eventually were able to express certain emotions, though having catastrophic grammar. They possessed a more violent temperament than the B1 model, to the point they would even strike down allied units in order to quickly intercept enemy targets, as seen in the First Battle of Geonosis. As well as that, they were also considerably more durable and intelligent, capable of easily withstanding light blaster bolts.<ref name="AOTC" />

Super battle droids were often retrofitted with adversarial specific parts. However, this method was introduced late in the war and had little effect on the outcome of the conflict. One known model change was the introduction of the [[B2 grapple droid/Legends|grapple droid]], which had heavier armor and a larger frame. This droid was programmed to be a close combat model able to receive primary lightsaber slashes and disable enemies through its electrified claws.<ref name="ROTS game">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' video game]]</ref> [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|Another specialized variant]] with fingered hands and additional sensors was involved in the release of the [[swamp gas]] toxin on [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]]. The [[D-60 assault droid]], another variant, was used in the [[Attack on Cartao|Battle of Cartao]] by CIS forces.<ref name="Hero of Cartao">{{InsiderCite|issue1=68|issue2=70|Hero of Cartao}}</ref> two [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpack]]-equipped variants of the droid, the [[B2-AA air assault super battle droid|jump droid]], and the [[B2-RP battle droid/Legends|rocket droid]], were also developed.<ref name="The Drop">{{CWACite|6|The Drop (comic story)}}</ref> Other variants included super battle droids armed with various weapons, such as the [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|Mortar Super Battle Droid]], the [[Anti-Air Super Battle Droid]], and the [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|Repeater super battle droid]]. A more heavily armed and armored version was the [[B2-HA super battle droid/Legends|Heavy super battle droid]], and [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|orray troopers]] were B2 droids armed with [[Flamethrower/Legends|flamethrowers]] which rode [[Orray/Legends|orrays]]. These variants were produced at Geonosian [[Barracks/Legends|troop center]]s.<ref name="SWGB:CC" />

[[File:B2_soldier.png|thumb|left|166x166px|A B2 soldier on Felucia.]]
During the [[third battle of Felucia]], the Separatist deployed an experimental model of super battle droid. This model was the [[B2 Assault]], which was an upgraded version of the preexisting B2-HA super droid. During the battle the CIS also deployed the B2 soldier, and this model of super battle droid was used to attack a Republic outpost staffed by [[Graul Company]], and these units had green markings.<ref name="CWAF">{{TCWA|loc=Felucia}}</ref>

The B2 battle droid was designed by the Techno Union using the existing B1 design as a template. After prototypes were successfully tested, [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] struck a deal with [[Poggle the Lesser/Legends|Poggle the Lesser]], [[Archduke/Legends|Archduke]] of Geonosis, to mass produce these droids.

[[File:CC_B-2_mount.jpg|thumb|180px|A [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2 unit]] mounted on an [[Orray/Legends|orray]].]]
Further orders were placed on worlds controlled by [[Baktoid Armor Workshop/Legends|Baktoid]] and quadrillions of B2s were soon running off the [[Geonosis droid factories/Legends|assembly lines]]. Despite their advantages and ease of production, however, they were not manufactured as extensively as their inferior cousins, the B1s.

During the Clone Wars, B2s would become an important component of the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]]. They participated in most battles in that conflict including the Battle of Geonosis, [[Battle of Muunilinst/Legends|Battle of Muunilinst]], [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]], and [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|Battle of Kashyyyk]], and innumerable others throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. B2s were used as shooting range targets as part of the training of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone]] [[Sniper/Legends|sharpshooters]].<ref name="Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Sharpshooter">{{SWArchive|url=games/playnow/sharpshooter|text=Sharpshooter|int=Sharpshooter (game)}}</ref>

A training model was used on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] for the training of [[Clone cadet/Legends|Clone cadets]].

[[R77]] served aboard the ''[[Invisible Hand/Legends|Invisible Hand]]''.<ref name="ROTSScrapbook">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Scrapbook]]''</ref> Following the [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|execution]] of the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] by [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious's]] new [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], the B2s were deactivated, along with the rest of the droid army.<ref name="ROTS" />

===Post-Clone Wars===
A few years after [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]], [[Gizor Dellso]] reactivated a [[Techno Union droid factory/Legends|droid factory]] on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]]. Among the reactivated production lines were a few lines that produced B2 battle droids, providing Dellso with an acceptable amount of B2's in his droid army.<ref name="BF2" />

After the Clone Wars, a few entrepreneurs found warehouses filled with the droids. Many were sold to gangs or major [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]] for enforcement. Others would be used by the various [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|Separatist holdouts]]. Like some B1 battle droids, B2s were also used as guards inside the [[Death Watch bunker]] on [[Endor/Legends|Endor]].<ref name="SWG">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref> [[Borvo]] the Hutt owned several super battle droids to defend his [[Borvo's Vault|vault]] on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name="SWG:ORDMBBD" />

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong]]'s invasion of the galaxy, many B2 droids used by the Galactic Alliance made up a force known as the [[Orange Panthacs]], which [[Battle of Mantessa|beat back]] an occupation force of [[Fire Breather]]s on [[Mantessa]].<ref name="TNEGtD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Super_droid.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Concept art from ''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones]]''.]]
B2 super battle droids first appeared in the [[2002]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Starfighter]]'', released shortly before [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']]''.<nowiki/>''

Animatics for ''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' show that the super battle droids were to dual wield [[E-5 blaster rifle/Legends|E-5 blaster rifles]], and not have built-in wrist blasters.<ref name="BlurayScene">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'', Disc 7, Star Wars Archives: Episode II Deleted Scene: Raid on the Droid Control Ship and Extended Arena Fight</ref>

In ''[[LEGO Star Wars III: The Clone Wars]]'', The rocket super battle droid fires regular rockets instead of pink ones.

In the ''Star Wars: Battlefront'' game series, the B2 super battle droids are deployed as standard infantry units, while B1 battle droids are in several specialized variants, as opposed to the B1s being more extensively utilized in the movies.

Although the B2 super battle droid's [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry indicated that the droid could operate without a master control signal,<ref name="Super battle droid droid in the Databank" /> in the ''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]'' mission "The [[Acclamator-class transgalactic military assault ship/Legends|RAS]] ''[[Prosecutor]]''", any B2 units remaining aboard the ''Prosecutor'' are deactivated once the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class Droid Control Ship]] is destroyed.<ref name="SW:RC">''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''</ref>

The video games ''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron]]'' and ''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Elite Squadron]]'' feature the labels "Super Battledroid Mk II" and "Super Battledroid Mk III" in the personalization editor, though the customization was up to the player.
